text:
Consider the given statement and decide which of the given assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement:

In the last year, Pune University has launched a number of vocational courses for the better future of students.

Assumptions:

A. Pune University believes that vocational education provides a better future for students.

B. Pune University is conscious about the future of students.
textHi:
दिए गए कथन पर विचार कीजिए और तय कीजिए कि दी गई कौन-सी धारणा कथन में निहित है/हैं।

कथन:

पिछले वर्ष में, पुणे विश्वविद्यालय ने छात्रों के बेहतर भविष्य के लिए कई व्यावसायिक पाठ्यक्रम शुरू किए हैं।

धारणाएँ:

A. पुणे विश्वविद्यालय का मानना है कि व्यावसायिक शिक्षा छात्रों के लिए बेहतर भविष्य प्रदान करती है।

B. पुणे विश्वविद्यालय छात्रों के भविष्य को लेकर सचेत है।
optionsHi: न तो धारणा A और न ही B निहित है।
धारणा A और B दोनों निहित हैं।
options: Neither assumption A nor B is implicit
Both assumptions A and B are implicit.
explanation: Both assumptions are implicit because the statement directly connects vocational courses to securing a better future, reflecting the university's concern and belief.

text:
Given is a statement followed by two assumptions numbered I and II. Consider the statement and the following assumptions and decide which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement.

Statement:

Sustainability can be defined as the practice of meeting the needs of the current generation without degrading or destroying the natural resources (e.g. water, soil, biodiversity, oil, minerals.)

Assumptions:

	Our lives and economies are dependent on natural capital, which is made up of these natural resources and natural services, and the energy provided by the sun.

	Just as every investor knows, we should invest our capital and live off on the interest, it provides. To live sustainably, we need to do the same: protect our natural capital and live off our biological income.
textHi:
एक कथन दिया गया है, जिसके बाद I और II क्रमांकित दो धारणाएँ दी गई हैं। कथन और निम्नलिखित धारणाओं पर विचार कीजिए और निर्णय कीजिए कि कौन सी धारणा/धारणाएँ कथनों में निहित है/हैं। 

कथन:

वर्तमान पीढ़ी की जरूरतों को बिना किसी प्राकृतिक संसाधन (जैसे-जल, मृदा, जैव विविधता, तेल, खनिजों) को नष्ट किए बिना पूरा करने को स्थायित्व के रूप में परिभाषित किया जा सकता है।

धारणा:

	हमारा जीवन और अर्थव्यवस्थाएँ प्राकृतिक पूंजी पर निर्भर हैं, जो इन प्राकृतिक संसाधनों और प्राकृतिक सेवाओं तथा सूर्य द्वारा प्रदान की गई ऊर्जा से बना है।

	चूँकि प्रत्येक निवेशक यह जानता है, कि हमें अपनी पूंजी निवेश करनी चाहिए और इससे मिलने वाले ब्याज का उपयोग करना चाहिए, जो हमें हमारी निवेश की गई पूंजी से प्राप्त होता है। सतत रूप से जीने के लिए, हमें यही करने की आवश्यकता है: प्राकृतिक पूंजी की रक्षा करें और जैविक आय से दूर रहें।
optionsHi: न तो धारणा I और न ही II निहित है।
I और II दोनों धारणा निहित हैं।
options: Neither assumption I nor II is implicit.
Both assumptions I and II are implicit.
explanation: Both assumptions logically follow and are necessary to support the concept of sustainability as defined in the statement regarding natural resources and capital.

text:
Directions: Answer the question given below

You are the secretary of your society and there is a new family wanting to take a house in the society, but you find out that they do not belong to your community and some people in your society are against letting them buy the house. What will you do?
textHi:
निर्देश: नीचे दिए गए प्रश्न का उत्तर दीजिए-

आप अपने समाज के सचिव हैं और एक नया परिवार है जो समाज में एक घर लेना चाहता है, लेकिन आपको पता चलता है कि वे आपके समुदाय के नहीं हैं और आपके समाज के कुछ लोग उनके घर खरीदने देने के खिलाफ हैं। आप क्या करेंगे?
optionsHi: एक कारण बनाएंगे और उन्हें घर खरीदने से रोक देंगे।
अपने समाज के सदस्यों को सांप्रदायिक सद्भाव के महत्व को समझाएंगे और परिवार को घर खरीदने देंगे।
परिवार को समझाएंगे कि वे समाज से संबंधित नहीं हैं।
परिवार को कहेंगे कि वे अपने समुदाय में घर खोजें।
options: Make up a reason and prohibit them from buying the house.
Explain to your society members the importance of communal harmony and let the family buy the house.
Explain the family that they do not belong in the society.
Tell the family to rather find a house in a society of their own community.
explanation: Upholding communal harmony and inclusivity is essential; you should educate the members and permit the family to purchase the house.

text: Gautam’s present age is equal to 20% of his father's age 15 years ago, and Gaurav's (brother of Gautam) present age is 60% of his father’s age 10 years ago. If the sum of Gautam’s present age and Gaurav’s present age is 31, then find their father’s present age.
textHi: गौतम की वर्तमान आयु 15 वर्ष पूर्व उसके पिता की आयु के 20% के बराबर है और गौरव (गौतम का भाई) की वर्तमान आयु 10 वर्ष पहले उसके पिता की आयु का 60% है। यदि गौतम की वर्तमान आयु और गौरव की वर्तमान आयु का योग 31 है, तो उनके पिता की वर्तमान आयु ज्ञात कीजिए।
explanation: Translating the ages into an algebraic equation yields 0.8F - 9 = 31, which means the father's present age is 50 years.

text:
Directions: A statement is followed by two inferences I and II. You have to consider the statement to be true even if it seems at variance from commonly known facts. You have to decide which of the given inferences, if any, follow from the given statement.

Statement: It was abandoning our nomadic lifestyle and then domesticating animals that brought about infectious diseases such as measles, small pox and tuberculosis.

Inferences:

I. Man prior to becoming settlers led a nomadic life.

II. The diseases such as measles, small pox and tuberculosis could be passed from one person to another.
textHi:
निर्देश: एक कथन के बाद दो अनुमान I और II दिए गये हैं। आपको दिए गये कथन को सत्य मानना है, भले ही वे सामान्यतः ज्ञात तथ्यों से भिन्न प्रतीत हो। आपको यह तय करना होगा कि दिए गए अनुमानों में से कौन सा दिए गये कथन का अनुसरण करता है।

कथन: यह हमारी खानाबदोश जीवन शैली त्यागना और फिर जीवों को पालतू बनाना, जो खसरा, चेचक और तपेदिक जैसे संक्रामक रोगों को लाते थे।

अनुमान:

I. बसने से पहले मनुष्य ने खानाबदोश जीवन व्यतीत किया।

II. खसरा, चेचक और तपेदिक जैसे रोग एक व्यक्ति से दूसरे व्यक्ति में पारित हो सकते हैं।
optionsHi: केवल अनुमान I अनुसरण करता है।
केवल अनुमान II अनुसरण करता है।
कोई भी अनुमान अनुसरण नहीं करता है।
explanation: Both inferences logically follow because abandoning a nomadic life implies they were nomadic before, and infectious diseases are by definition communicable.

text: Triangle ABC is right angled at B. BD is an altitude on AC. If AD = 5 cm and DC = 9 cm, what is the length (in cm) of BD?

text:
Direction: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow:

Anyone who has travelled by road through the older counties of England will have noticed that the towns there have a shape nobody can have intended. They are long and they are thin. A settlement which ought by its population to occupy a compact square of a mile or so instead straggles for four or five miles along a single highway, one plot deep upon either side, with open fields beginning immediately behind the back gardens. The pattern repeats itself across districts that differ in soil, in trade and in age, which is reason enough to think it no accident; and it was certainly the result of no plan.

It followed instead from a rule about the individual plot. A builder could not lawfully put up a house that had no frontage upon an existing public road, because the local authority would not adopt a new street until houses already stood along it, and would not carry water or drainage to a house that stood upon no adopted street. Taken by itself the rule was a defensible one. It prevented the scattering of dwellings across open country where no service could reach them, and it placed the cost of making up a street upon the man who stood to profit by building in it.

What it also did was to make the land beside an existing road worth several times the land fifty yards behind it, although the two were in every physical respect identical. No builder who had a choice would build behind. Each of them, acting sensibly and well within the rule, added a house to the ribbon; and the ribbon lengthened year upon year until the cost of carrying a water main, a sewer, a postman and a fire engine from one end of it to the other had come to exceed the whole of the saving the rule had been framed to secure.

Nobody chose the outcome and nobody broke the rule. That is the part worth carrying away, and it is not a point about roads at all. A regulation addressed to the individual case is answered individually, and the shape of the aggregate is then nobody's decision. It does not follow that such rules are bad ones. It follows only that their consequences cannot be read off from their purposes, and that the body which frames a rule is seldom the body which notices what the rule has produced.

Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions that follow.

explanation: The central argument highlights that individual actions responding to specific rules lead to an aggregate outcome that was never intentionally designed.

text:
Directions: The five sentences below, labelled (A) to (E), are not in order. Rearrange them into a meaningful paragraph and answer the questions.

(A) A loose sheet can be taken out and another put in its place, and nobody looking at the book afterwards is able to tell that it has been done.

(B) The constable's notebook was for a long time no more than a pad of loose paper carried about in the pocket of his tunic.

(C) Bound and numbered books were therefore made compulsory, and a missing page became in itself a thing that had to be explained.

(D) Defence counsel soon learnt to ask whether the notes produced in court were in fact the notes that had first been written.

(E) The question could not be answered either way, and evidence that may well have been sound was lost upon that account alone.

What is the correct order of the sentences?
explanation: The paragraph logically flows from describing loose paper notebooks (B), explaining how sheets could be swapped (A), mentioning defense counsel questioning notes (D), the resulting loss of evidence (E), to the mandatory bound books solution (C).
